title: Health in depth
goal: Describe symptoms precisely and say how long you have had them, mention allergies and conditions, follow a doctor's instructions and deal with appointments and hospitals.
intro:
Unit 9 got you as far as **माझं डोकं दुखतंय**. This unit is for when you actually have to sit in front of a doctor in Pune or Mumbai and explain: what exactly is wrong (**मला चक्कर येतेय**, **अंगात कणकण आहे**), **since when** (**दोन दिवसांपासून**), what you're allergic to, and then understand what the doctor tells you to do.

The grammar is the two things every consultation needs: saying how long something has been going on — Marathi uses the **present tense + -पासून** where English says 'I have been…' — and following instructions, including the doctor's favourite form **ही गोळी जेवणानंतर घ्यायची** 'this tablet is to be taken after food'.

grammar.title: 'For' and 'since': -पासून with the present tense
grammar.body:
English says 'I **have had** a fever for two days', 'I**'ve been** coughing since Monday' — a present perfect. Marathi looks at it the other way round: the fever **is** still here, so it uses the plain **present** (or the present continuous) plus **-पासून** 'from':

दोन दिवसां**पासून** मला ताप **आहे** 'I've had a fever for two days'.
सोमवार**पासून** खोकला **येतोय** 'I've been coughing since Monday'.

The time word goes into the oblique before -पासून: दिवस → दिवसांपासून, आठवडा → आठवड्यापासून, महिना → महिन्यापासून, वर्ष → वर्षांपासून; and कालपासून, सकाळपासून, रात्रीपासून. 'For' and 'since' are the same word. Ask **कधीपासून?** 'since when?' or **किती दिवसांपासून?** 'for how many days?'.

**'It's been … since'**: the **-ऊन** form of the event + the time + **झाले / झाला**: ताप **येऊन** तीन दिवस **झाले** 'it's been three days since the fever started', ऑपरेशन **होऊन** एक महिना **झाला** 'it's been a month since the operation'. Very common in speech.

**'For the last …'**: **गेले** दोन दिवस मला झोप नाही 'for the last two days I haven't slept'.

**'Ago'** is a finished event, so it takes the past: दोन दिवसां**पूर्वी** ताप **आला** 'the fever came two days ago'.

**The trap:** don't put a situation that's still going on in the past. दोन दिवसांपासून ताप **होता** means 'I had had a fever for two days' — it's over. If you still have it, say **आहे** / **येतोय**.

examples.en: I've had a headache for three days.
I've had diarrhoea since last night.
Mum has been diabetic for ten years.
It's been four days since the fever started.

examples.native: गेले दोन आठवडे मला नीट झोप लागत नाहीये.
examples.roman: gele don āṭhavḍe malā nīṭ dzhop lāgat nāhīye.
examples.en: For the last two weeks I haven't been sleeping properly.

grammar.title: Following instructions: घ्या, घ्यायची, -ऊ नका and how often
grammar.body:
Doctors and chemists give instructions in three ways, and you'll hear all three in one visit.

**1. Polite command (-आ)**: ही गोळी **घ्या**, आराम **करा**, भरपूर पाणी **प्या**.

**2. 'Is to be …': stem + आयचा / आयची / आयचं** — the most common way a doctor explains a prescription. It agrees with the **medicine**, not with you: ही गोळी (f) जेवणानंतर **घ्यायची** 'this tablet is to be taken after food', हे सिरप (n) रात्री **घ्यायचं**, हा डोस (m) **चुकवायचा नाही** 'this dose is not to be missed'. With no object it's neuter: पाच दिवस बाहेरचं **खायचं नाही**. (Leaflets and written prescriptions use **-आवी / -आवे**: घ्यावी.)

**3. Don't: stem + ऊ + नका** (तुम्ही) / **नकोस** (तू): थंड पाणी **पिऊ नका**, गाडी **चालवू नका**.

**How often and when**
- दिवसातून **एकदा / दोनदा / तीनदा** 'once / twice / three times a day' (or एक वेळा, दोन वेळा).
- **दर** सहा तासांनी 'every six hours', **दर** दोन दिवसांनी 'every other day'.
- **सकाळ-संध्याकाळ** 'morning and evening', **रात्री झोपताना** 'at bedtime' (-ताना from Unit 30).
- जेवणा**आधी** 'before food', जेवणा**नंतर** 'after food', **उपाशीपोटी** 'on an empty stomach'.
- **पाच दिवस** 'for five days' — no word for 'for'.

Indian prescriptions often write the schedule as **1-0-1** (morning – afternoon – night): that means one tablet in the morning, none in the afternoon, one at night.

**The trap:** -आयचा agreement follows the thing taken: गोळी घ्याय**ची**, सिरप / इंजेक्शन घ्याय**चं**, डोस घ्याय**चा**.

examples.en: Take this tablet three times a day.
This medicine is to be taken at bedtime.

examples.native: दर सहा तासांनी दोन चमचे सिरप घ्या.
examples.roman: dar sahā tāsānnī don tsamche sirap ghyā.
examples.en: Take two spoons of syrup every six hours.

examples.native: पाच दिवस तेलकट काही खायचं नाही.
examples.roman: pāts divas telkaṭ kāhī khāytsaṃ nāhī.
examples.en: No oily food for five days.

dialogue.title: At the family doctor
dialogue.setting: Rohan has been unwell for two days and goes to Dr Gokhale's clinic in Kothrud, Pune.

lines.speaker: Dr Gokhale
lines.en: Have a seat. What's the problem?

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: डॉक्टर, दोन दिवसांपासून ताप आहे आणि अंग खूप दुखतंय.
lines.roman: ḍôkṭar, don divasāmpāsūn tāp āhe āṇi aṅg khūp dukhtaṃy.
lines.en: Doctor, I've had a fever for two days and my whole body aches.

lines.speaker: Dr Gokhale
lines.en: How high is it? Did you take your temperature?

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: काल रात्री एकशे दोन होता. आज सकाळपासून थोडा कमी आहे.
lines.roman: kāl rātrī ekshe don hotā. ādz sakāḷpāsūn thoḍā kamī āhe.
lines.en: Last night it was a hundred and two. Since this morning it's a bit lower.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: नाही, पण थोडी मळमळ आहे आणि उठल्यावर चक्कर येते.
lines.roman: nāhī, paṇ thoḍī maḷmaḷ āhe āṇi uṭhlyāvar tsakkar yete.
lines.en: No, but I feel a bit sick, and I get dizzy when I get up.

lines.speaker: Dr Gokhale
lines.native: बघू… घसा पण लाल आहे. कशाची ॲलर्जी आहे का?
lines.roman: baghū… ghasā paṇ lāl āhe. kashāchī ælarjī āhe kā?
lines.en: Let's see… your throat's red too. Are you allergic to anything?

lines.speaker: Dr Gokhale
lines.native: व्हायरल वाटतंय. पण उद्या रक्ताची तपासणी करून घ्या, डेंग्यू नाही ना ते बघू.
lines.roman: vhāyral vāṭtaṃy. paṇ udyā raktāchī tapāsṇī karūn ghyā, ḍeṅgyū nāhī nā te baghū.
lines.en: It looks viral. But get a blood test done tomorrow, so we can rule out dengue.

lines.speaker: Dr Gokhale
lines.native: ही तापाची गोळी दिवसातून तीनदा, जेवणानंतर घ्यायची. आणि ही फक्त रात्री झोपताना.
lines.roman: hī tāpāchī goḷī divasātūn tīndā, jevaṇānantar ghyāychī. āṇi hī phakta rātrī dzhoptānā.
lines.en: This fever tablet three times a day, after food. And this one only at bedtime.

lines.speaker: Dr Gokhale
lines.native: हलकं जेवण — खिचडी, वरण-भात. तेलकट, तिखट काही नको. आणि भरपूर पाणी प्या.
lines.roman: halkaṃ jevaṇ — khichḍī, varaṇ-bhāt. telkaṭ, tikhaṭ kāhī nako. āṇi bharpūr pāṇī pyā.
lines.en: Light food — khichdi, dal and rice. Nothing oily or spicy. And drink plenty of water.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.en: Thank you, doctor. How much do I owe you?

culture:
Most Maharashtrian families have a **फॅमिली डॉक्टर** with a small **दवाखाना** (clinic) in the neighbourhood: you walk in without an appointment, wait your turn, and often the doctor hands over the medicines in small paper packets with the schedule written on them, or writes **1-0-1** on the prescription. Chemists (called **मेडिकल**, as in *जवळचं मेडिकल कुठे आहे?*) will sell many medicines over the counter and are a first stop for small problems. Doctors are spoken of in the respectful plural: **डॉक्टर आले आहेत**, **डॉक्टरांनी सांगितलं**.

The monsoon brings a season of **व्हायरल** fever, dengue and malaria, so a fever that lasts more than two or three days usually means a blood test. Expect relatives to give advice too: **हळदीचं दूध** (milk with turmeric), गरम पाण्याच्या **गुळण्या** (salt-water gargles) and a strict **पथ्य** — no curd, nothing cold, nothing fried, and **मऊ भात** or **खिचडी** until you're better.

When someone is in hospital, visiting is expected: people take fruit, sit for a while and ask **आता कसं वाटतंय?**. Most private hospitals in Pune and Mumbai deal with health insurance directly (**कॅशलेस**), but ask the desk before you're admitted.

tip.title: Saying what's wrong
tip.body:
- Most symptoms happen *to* you (Unit 30): **मला** चक्कर **येते**, खाज **येतेय**, जुलाब **होतायत**.
- Something that has appeared: **आलं / आली आहे**: पुरळ **आलंय**, सूज **आली आहे**.
- The verb agrees with the symptom: चक्कर (f) येते, अशक्तपणा (m) आलाय.
- Some are verbs in their own right: **मळमळतंय** 'I feel sick'.

sentences.en: I feel dizzy when I get up in the morning.
Whenever I eat anything I feel sick.
My son has diarrhoea.
My foot has swollen up.

sentences.native: हातावर पुरळ आलंय आणि खूप खाज येतेय.
sentences.roman: hātāvar puraḷ ālaṃy āṇi khūp khādz yetey.
sentences.en: I've got a rash on my arm and it's really itchy.
I've been feeling very weak since the fever.
Are these symptoms of dengue?
I always feel sick on buses.
My eyes are itchy.

tip.title: -पासून: for and since
tip.body:
- Still going on? Use the **present** + **-पासून**: दोन दिवसां**पासून** ताप **आहे** 'I've had a fever for two days'.
- Time word in the oblique: दिवसांपासून, आठवड्यापासून, कालपासून, सकाळपासून.
- Ask **कधीपासून?** or **किती दिवसांपासून?**
- Or: ताप येऊन तीन दिवस **झाले** 'it's been three days since…'. 'Ago' is **-पूर्वी** + past.

sentences.en: I've had a cough since yesterday.
How many days have you had a fever?
My back has been hurting for a week.

sentences.native: सकाळपासून अंगदुखी आहे आणि थोडी कणकण पण.
sentences.roman: sakāḷpāsūn aṅgdukhī āhe āṇi thoḍī kaṇkaṇ paṇ.
sentences.en: Since this morning I've had body aches, and I'm a bit feverish too.
How long have you had this itch?
It's been three days since the diarrhoea started.

sentences.native: दोन दिवसांपूर्वी ताप आला होता, आता बरा आहे.
sentences.roman: don divasāmpūrvī tāp ālā hotā, ātā barā āhe.
sentences.en: I had a fever two days ago, now I’m fine. (man)

sentences.native: गेले दोन दिवस मी काहीच खाल्लं नाही.
sentences.roman: gele don divas mī kāhīts khāllaṃ nāhī.
sentences.en: I haven't eaten anything for the last two days.
I've been living in Pune for five years. (man)

sentences.native: बोला, काय त्रास होतोय? किती दिवसांपासून?
sentences.roman: bolā, kāy trās hotoy? kitī divasāmpāsūn?
sentences.en: Tell me, what's the trouble? For how many days?
I'm allergic to penicillin.

sentences.native: माझ्या वडिलांना शुगर आहे, ते गोड खात नाहीत.
sentences.roman: mājhyā vaḍilānnā shugar āhe, te goḍ khāt nāhīt.
sentences.en: My father is diabetic, he doesn't eat sweets.
Grandma's blood pressure has gone up.

When will I get the test report?

The wound is bleeding.

sentences.roman: tumhālā kuṭhlyā aushadhāchī ælarjī āhe kā?
sentences.en: Are you allergic to any medicine?

lessons.title: Taking your medicine

tip.title: Instructions: घ्या, घ्यायची, -ऊ नका
tip.body:
- Polite command: ही गोळी **घ्या**, आराम **करा**.
- 'Is to be taken': stem + **आयचा / आयची / आयचं**, agreeing with the medicine: गोळी घ्याय**ची**, सिरप घ्याय**चं**.
- Don't: stem + ऊ **नका**: थंड पाणी पिऊ **नका**.
- How often: दिवसातून **दोनदा**, **दर** सहा तासांनी, जेवणा**नंतर**.

new: ही गोळी दिवसातून दोनदा, जेवणानंतर घ्यायची.

sentences.en: This tablet is to be taken in the morning on an empty stomach.
This syrup is to be taken twice a day.

sentences.native: दर आठ तासांनी एक गोळी घ्या.
sentences.roman: dar āṭh tāsānnī ek goḷī ghyā.
sentences.en: Take one tablet every eight hours.
Don't miss a single dose.

sentences.native: औषध पाच दिवस घ्या, मध्येच बंद करू नका.
sentences.roman: aushadh pāts divas ghyā, madhyets band karū nakā.
